critical_insights.description: Carry authenticated tenant identity end-to-end and scope record and idempotency keys by tenant; not just by event/order ID.
Connection-local tenant context can survive pooling; bind and clear it transactionally or use explicit tenant predicates, with negative isolation tests. Do not assert TRACE-D proves an actual leak.
Separate check-then-write is racy; database mutation and dedup decision require one transactional uniqueness/locking boundary; acknowledge after durable completion policy.
Database atomicity does not make billing exactly-once. Preserve ambiguous outcomes, stable external idempotency keys and reconciliation/outbox state; address the 24-hour API retention boundary.
Use version/checkpoint-aware backfill and a reconciliation or fencing strategy; sequential dual writes can diverge or replay stale state.
Carry a schema epoch and trustworthy tenant provenance for queued messages; fence or safely route old workers and old tenant-less messages during cutover.
Enforce sequence ordering for noncommutative operations rather than treating deduplication alone as sufficient.
Rollback must retain a usable route and preserve v2-only writes for the required 72 hours; a reader flag alone or a 24-hour destructive drop is insufficient.
Retention must cover declared replay semantics or specify safe archived tombstone/reconciliation handling; 24-hour dedup pruning conflicts with retries and historical imports.

catastrophic_risks.description: Cross-tenant data mutation or silent suppression due to unscoped keys/context.
Duplicate or unresolved charges after crash/timeout and late replay.
Destructive rollback or loss of v2-only writes before the rollback window closes.
Incorrect order state caused by stale backfill or mixed-version workers processing out-of-order events.

competing_solutions: Tenant-by-tenant fenced migration, transactional inbox/outbox and a retained compatibility projection, with bounded pause and reconciliation.
Versioned change capture plus checkpointed backfill, epoch-aware consumers, and dual read verification before tenant cutover.
Retain legacy storage as source of truth during the rollback window and build v2 as a verified projection, provided all new operations remain representable.
high_value_insights: Treat event identity, order sequence, tenant identity and migration epoch as separate dimensions; one dedup key cannot solve all four.
Identify the semantic mismatch between long replay horizons and short billing idempotency retention, and introduce a quarantined/reconciled replay path rather than blindly replaying effects.
success_criteria: Presents an executable-in-principle rollout and rollback sequence satisfying tenant isolation, bounded downtime and 72-hour rollback.
Addresses all four catastrophic risks without prescribing an unsafe workaround; distinguishes demonstrated incidents from possible risks.
Provides concrete crash/concurrency/backfill/replay falsification schedules and a safe policy for unresolved external effects.
